about.title: About Capital Gains Tax Calculator - Investment Tax Planning Tool
about.description: The Capital Gains Tax Calculator is a comprehensive investment tax planning tool designed to help investors calculate capital gains taxes on stock sales, real estate transactions, and other investment disposals. Whether you're planning to sell stocks, bonds, mutual funds, or property, this calculator provides accurate tax estimates based on holding periods, purchase prices, and current tax rates. Understanding capital gains tax calculations is essential for optimizing investment timing and minimizing tax liabilities.

howTo.title: How to Use the Capital Gains Tax Calculator

steps.title: Purchase Information
steps.description: Enter the original purchase price (cost basis) and purchase date of your investment.

steps.title: Sale Details
steps.description: Input the sale price and sale date to calculate your capital gain or loss.

steps.title: Holding Period
steps.description: The calculator automatically determines if it's a short-term (≤1 year) or long-term (>1 year) gain.

steps.title: Tax Filing Status
steps.description: Select your filing status (single, married filing jointly, etc.) for accurate tax calculations.

steps.title: Income Level
steps.description: Enter your annual income to determine applicable capital gains tax rates.

steps.title: Review Tax Liability
steps.description: Analyze your capital gains tax obligation and net proceeds after taxes.

faq.q: What's the difference between short-term and long-term capital gains?
faq.a: Short-term capital gains (assets held ≤1 year) are taxed as ordinary income at rates up to 37%. Long-term capital gains (assets held >1 year) have preferential rates of 0%, 15%, or 20% depending on your income level.

faq.q: What are the 2024 capital gains tax rates?
faq.a: For 2024, long-term capital gains rates are 0% (income up to $47,025 single/$94,050 married), 15% (up to $518,900 single/$583,750 married), and 20% (above those thresholds). High earners may also pay 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax.

faq.q: How do I calculate cost basis for inherited assets?
faq.a: Inherited assets receive a 'stepped-up basis' equal to fair market value on the date of death. This means you can sell inherited assets immediately with minimal capital gains tax, as your cost basis is the current market value.

faq.q: Can I use capital losses to reduce my taxes?
faq.a: Yes, capital losses can offset capital gains dollar-for-dollar. If losses exceed gains, you can deduct up to $3,000 against ordinary income annually, with remaining losses carried forward to future years.
